children: Collaboration with leading broadcasters, mobile operators, and technology partners explores how open network APIs can transform 5G into a predictable and prioritized resource for live production workflows

, a leading global provider of mission-critical, real-time video networking and visual collaboration solutions, today announced its participation in the IBC Accelerator Media Innovation Programme as part of the Network Control: Your Connection, Your Choice project.

The IBC Accelerator Media Innovation Programme brings together broadcasters, service providers, technology companies, and academic institutions to explore innovative solutions to some of the media industry's most complex challenges. The

params.linkText: Network Control: Your Connection, Your Choice project

children: is focused on investigating how open network APIs can help applications with specialised requirements interact with standardised network capabilities designed to meet defined quality requirements, supporting reliable and business-critical media production workflows over 5G.

The project is led by a group of industry Champions including BBC, EBU, DAZN, France Télévisions, GSMA, RAI Italy, RTL Germany, TV 2 Denmark, Vodafone, and Telefónica. Haivision joins fellow Participants Neutral Wireless, LiveU, SliceFinity, and Vonage, alongside Academic Partner University of Strathclyde, in developing and testing proof-of-concept workflows around major sporting events in Germany and Spain for demonstration and discussion at IBC2026.

As part of the initiative, the project team is evaluating how network-aware applications and open network APIs can provide broadcasters and content creators with greater visibility and control over connectivity resources. The goal is to enable more reliable and consistent transmission of live video over 5G networks, helping media organisations improve the quality and resilience of their remote and mobile production workflows.

Haivision is providing its expertise in live video contribution and mobile video transmission technologies to help assess the role of programmable Quality on Demand network capabilities in supporting high-quality, low latency video transport over 5G in demanding production environments. The project leverages Haivision's Falkon X2 mobile video transmitter, a compact bonded cellular field unit designed for live sports, news, and remote production workflows, combined with the Haivision StreamHub receiver and Haivision Hub 360 cloud master control solution to enable API-driven requests for specific SIMs to prioritize traffic when network conditions become congested.

“We are delighted that Haivision is supporting the Network Control Accelerator project. It’s an unprecedented collaboration between leading mobile operators in Germany, European broadcasters, and the vendor ecosystem that will deliver some powerful learnings for both sectors regarding Quality on Demand APIs for live broadcast operations at large scale sports and live events,” said Mark Smith, who heads the IBC Accelerator Programme. “Haivision has been a foundational supporter of the Programme since its inception in 2019, and we have seen some of our 5G projects deliver astonishing, groundbreaking innovation for the industry.”

“As 5G is becoming the norm for cellular networks to support remote and live production workflows, ensuring predictable and reliable connectivity is becoming more important than ever,” said Jean-Marc Racine, Chief Product Officer at Haivision. “Through the IBC Accelerator Programme, we are collaborating with industry leaders to explore how programmable 5G services and open Quality on Demand network APIs can enhance live video contribution and provide greater operational confidence for broadcasters in challenging environments covering live sports, news, and events.”
Haivision and the IBC Accelerator Programme at IBC2026

Visitors to IBC2026 can learn more about Haivision’s live video contribution solutions and its participation in the IBC Accelerator program by visiting the Haivision stand (Hall 2, Stand 2.B32) and IBC Accelerator Zone (Hall 14, Future Tech, Stand 14.D25). The showcase of the Network Control Project will take place on the Future Tech Stage in Hall 14 from 11:30am to 12.30pm on Sunday, September 13.
To schedule a meeting with Haivision at IBC2026, visit: https://www.haivision.com/events/ibc/

Haivision is a leading global provider of mission-critical, real-time video networking and visual collaboration solutions. Haivision enables organizations globally to engage audiences, enhance collaboration, and support decision-making. We provide high-quality, low-latency, secure, and reliable live video at a global scale. Haivision open-sourced its award-winning SRT low-latency video streaming protocol and founded the SRT Alliance to support its adoption. Awarded four Emmys® for Technology and Engineering from the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences, Haivision continues to fuel the future of IP video transformation. Founded in 2004, Haivision is headquartered in Montreal and Chicago with offices, sales, and support located throughout the Americas, Europe, and Asia.
